title: Lesson 1 · AI foundations
kit: Most of this room already uses AI at work, in more than one tool. Before we build anything, one question: what is it actually doing when it answers?
Know what it does and where it fails.
Explain what generative AI does well and where it can be wrong.
chrome: By the end of this block:

title: What is AI?
kit: Your answers stay on the screen. Next, we see what AI really does.

title: A very well-read new joiner.
kit: It has read more than any associate ever will, so its drafts are fast and fluent. It has never seen this client's file, so it fills gaps with what is usual.

title: What it really does.
kit: A model trained on very large amounts of text that writes by predicting the most likely next word, one word at a time. That is why it reads, summarizes, extracts and drafts well.
Like the new joiner's fluent first draft…
…each word is likely. Likely is not the same as checked.
It predicts. It does not look things up unless you give it the source.

title: It writes by guessing the next word.
kit: It writes by guessing the next word.
At each step, every possible next word gets a score. The model picks one, adds it, and predicts again.
It predicts likely words. It does not check if they are true.
The cut-off test for Abdali Foods shows the invoice was posted in
chrome: What word comes next? Click one.
Now it predicts again, using the whole sentence so far
so it is a cut-off point.

title: Fluent and wrong.
kit: When AI writes something that sounds right but is not true: a wrong amount, date, name or source, written with full confidence.
…that nobody has ticked yet. Professional skepticism applies.
Tick every figure against the source document.

title: Confident, fluent and made up.
kit: The AI was wrong, and the people paid. Check before anyone relies on it.
Sources: Mata v. Avianca, Inc., No. 22-cv-1461 (S.D.N.Y., 22 June 2023); Moffatt v. Air Canada, 2024 BCCRT 149 (14 February 2024).
Two lawyers used ChatGPT to find past cases for a client's claim against an airline. It invented the cases and their quotes, and said they were real. The lawyers did not check.
The judge fined the two lawyers and their firm $5,000.
A refund rule the airline never had
Air Canada's website chatbot told a customer, whose grandmother had just died, that he could ask for a lower bereavement fare after his flight. The airline's real policy said no.
Air Canada said the chatbot was responsible for its own words. The tribunal disagreed, and the airline paid.

Attach the source file. Then check the answer against it.
Role: who Claude is, and the job in one line.

title: A prompt is not a process.
kit: A prompt is not a process.
Even a good prompt lives in one chat, and you type it again next time. A repeatable method keeps the same input, rules and output shape, so every run can be reviewed the same way.

title: From a chat to an agent.
kit: From a chat to an agent.

An agent is AI set up to do one job the same way every time. Its instructions are saved, it reads the files it needs, it returns a fixed output, and it can run without you. Today you build one in Claude.
A chat answers one question, once…
…an agent does one job, every week, from a written method.
Chat is for questions. Agents are for repeated work.
